characteristics: Multi-missile system: ranges from 40km (9M96) up to 400km (40N6E)
engages aircraft, cruise and ballistic missiles
Strength: Longest engagement envelope of any system in this catalog; integrates with Buk/Pantsir into a single layered network
Limitation: Extremely expensive per battery; primarily a homeland/rear-area asset rather than something used far forward near the line
Estimated quantity available: Estimated 50-60+ battalions in Russian service pre-war (exact current operational count not fully disclosed)
employment_notes: Anchors Russia's own multi-layer IADS (integrated air defense system) — the same layered logic (long/medium/short + hard-kill/soft-kill) both sides converge on independently, worth pairing with Ukraine's Patriot/NASAMS/IRIS-T/Gepard stack as a direct comparison
contrast_vs_traditional: S-400 doctrine was built to deny an opposing air force freedom of maneuver at long range against manned aircraft and ballistic threats — a genuinely different problem from the thousands of small, cheap drones now also filling the sky, many flying below or beneath the economic threshold a system this expensive was ever meant to engage. That gap is exactly why a short-range layer like Tor-M2 sits underneath it doing the day-to-day work, not because the long-range system failed at its actual job.

notes: Specs meet the bar but the unit cost is an estimate — cost is not verified.
